name: New Hampshire
nameStory: Named by Captain John Mason for Hampshire, England, where he had lived. The phrase everyone actually remembers, 'Live Free or Die,' came much later - from a toast General John Stark sent to a veterans' reunion in 1809 when he was too ill to attend.
capitalStory: Concord is named after an actual concord: the settlement of a long, bitter boundary war between rival towns. The capital of New Hampshire is named for the moment people finally stopped arguing.

majorFeatures.name: White Mountains
majorFeatures.note: The highest range in the Northeast

majorFeatures.name: Mount Washington
majorFeatures.note: Famous for the worst weather in America

majorFeatures.name: Merrimack River
majorFeatures.note: Powered the mill towns of the 1800s

funFacts: A wind gust of 231 mph was recorded on Mount Washington in 1934 and stood as the world record for surface wind for over 60 years.
New Hampshire has about 18 miles of ocean coastline, the shortest of any coastal state.
The 1944 Bretton Woods conference, held at a New Hampshire resort, set up the financial system that ran the postwar world.
Three climate zones collide over Mount Washington, which is why its weather is so violent.
whyItMatters: New Hampshire has held the first presidential primary in the nation since 1920. A state with about 0.4% of the US population gets an outsized first look at every candidate, which both parties argue about constantly.
